summary.en: One small ending tells you who did it.

body.en:
Russian past tense is friendly. There is one form per verb, and its ending shows who or what it is about. Nothing else changes.

| Who | Ending | Form of "to be" |
|---|---|---|
| he | -л | он был |
| she | -ла | она была |
| it | -ло | оно было |
| we, you, they | -ли | они были |

The ending follows the person speaking, too. A man says **я был**, a woman says **я была**. Ainura, who says "I used to be a vegetarian too", uses the feminine form.

**было** is also the form for "there was": **не было денег** means "there was no money". In the present tense Russian simply leaves out "to be", so these forms are how "was" and "were" show up.
